title: What If the Whole Asteroid Belt Became One Planet?

scenes.text: What if the whole asteroid belt became one planet? It would be smaller than Pluto.
The belt holds millions of rocks between Mars and Jupiter. You'd think that's a lot of material.
It isn't. All of it together weighs only about four percent of the Moon's mass.
Nearly half of that sits in just four objects: Ceres, Vesta, Pallas and Hygiea.
Squash it all together at Ceres's density, and you get a ball with a radius of about 700 kilometers.
Pluto's radius is 1,188 kilometers. The belt was never a failed planet. There was never enough material.
